Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool onboarding intent + SLA targets (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the time today, Elena / Marcus — appreciate the candid rundown of the production constraints and timeline. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can align with procurement and your infra team.

Key pain points you highlighted
- Model latency spikes during morning batch inference windows (95th pctl approaching 1.9s per token) that impact the clinician triage UI.
- Data isolation requirements: all inference must run in a logically isolated GPU pool with strict VPC peering and no shared tenant routing.
- Predictable throughput for nightly bulk jobs (up to ~2.5M tokens/hr) with headroom for 30% burst on weekdays.

Goals we heard
- Dedicated GPU pool (single-tenant) deployed in us-west with strict network isolation and KMS integration.
- SLA target: 99.95% availability for the dedicated pool and 95th-pctl latency <1.2s for typical 256-token requests.
- Delivery window: pilot in 4–6 weeks, production ramp over 8–12 weeks once committed.

Redwood suggested configuration (high level)
- Dedicated capacity: 6x A100s (reserved) + 2x burst nodes for peak windows.
- Autoscaling policy: target latency-driven scaling with pre-warmed warm-standby nodes for night runs.
- Network/security: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS + audit log forwarding to your SIEM.

Attachments sent with this note:
- CloudVerge_dedicated_estimate_v1.pdf (cost breakdown + capacity profile)
- mutual-action-plan_CVH.docx (milestones / approval owners)

Open questions / decisions needed from CloudVerge
1) Finalize committed GPU count (we proposed 6 reserved + 2 burst; confirm if you want additional headroom).
2) Confirm procurement timeline and PO owner so we can draft the Reserved Capacity agreement.
3) Any additional compliance evidence (SOC2 artifact / pen test) required before a pilot starts.

Next steps (agreed on call)
- Redwood: share this recap + updated estimate and MAP (attached) — action: Aditya (today).
- CloudVerge: share PO owner and procurement timeline — action: Marcus (by Tue 21 Jul).
- Redwood CS/Infra: schedule a technical onboarding session focused on VPC/KMS with CloudVerge infra — action: Priyom (propose slots).

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, call it out and I will update. Otherwise I will follow up with a short SOW + draft contract to start procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Committed capacity: we are comfortable with 6 reserved GPUs to start but would like an option to increase to 8 within the first quarter without a long lead time. Please add quarterly true-up language to the MAP.
2) SLA: the 99.95% availability is acceptable; for latency we need a 95th-pctl guarantee at the 256-token size as you wrote. Can Redwood provide examples of how you calculate token-level latency (sampling windows / p95 vs p99 callouts)?
3) Compliance evidence: we will need the SOC 2 Type II report and recent pen-test exec summary before procurement signs off.

Procurement: adding procurement@cloudvergehealth.com to the thread. Their initial ask — can you share a 1-page order summary + payment terms? They prefer Net-45 for first-time vendors.

We are good to proceed with a pilot as soon as procurement receives the one-pager. Forwarding procurement to follow up on commercial points.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudVerge Health
